memory_candidates: CSLib DerivationTree idiom: to lift a closed axiom instance (Deriv Axioms [] phi via .ax [] _ h) into a nonempty context Gamma, must explicitly weaken (weakening_deriv or .weakening [] _ _ ... (by simp)) -- .ax's context argument does NOT auto-generalize.

Hilbert-style proof pattern: derivable_imp_trans (transitivity of Derivable-implication, composing two closed A-imp-B / B-imp-C facts via a single-hypothesis context + assumption/weakening/mp/impIntro) is a broadly reusable combinator for chained Hilbert derivations -- worth considering for promotion into shared CSLib Metalogic infra if more tasks need it.

When a source text (Simpson 1994) asserts a formula is 'derived by repeated application of axiom X' without giving the sub-derivation, do not assume a single flat instantiation of axiom X suffices -- check by hand whether the naive substitution's consequent actually matches the target (it did not for formula 6.8: naive hFS instantiation produces box(phi imp psi), not the target box psi, and bridging requires a genuine induction, not a bare IPL fact, once the antecedent contains a diamond-guarded tail).
